reflections.summary: Leaving Mega Swampert and Pelipper on the bench left the team without weather control against Sun. In Game 2, adjusting to a slow Trick Room mode backfired because fast Chlorophyll Sleep Powder from Venusaur repeatedly disrupted setup, while an early Stone Edge miss allowed Mega Charizard Y and Kingambit to heavily damage our leads before Trick Room could yield effective offense.
reflections.adjustment: In preparation, register Mega Swampert and Pelipper from the roster to contest weather against Mega Charizard Y and turn off Chlorophyll. At Team Preview, avoid leading slow setup mons directly into Sun plus Sleep Powder pressure without sleep immunity (e.g., Tsareena or Safety Goggles support).
reflections.notebook: Opponent sets revealed: Charizard-Mega-Y (Timid: Heat Wave, Solar Beam, Air Slash, Protect), Venusaur (Modest, Focus Sash, Chlorophyll: Energy Ball, Sludge Bomb, Sleep Powder, Protect), Kingambit (Adamant, BlackGlasses: Kowtow Cleave, Iron Head, Sucker Punch, Protect). Strategic takeaways: Sun + Chlorophyll Sleep Powder invalidates passive Trick Room setup without sleep blocking or weather disruption; Rain support (Pelipper/Mega Swampert) is required for weather override.

reflections.summary: Won game 2 and the series 2-0 because Mega Charizard Y plus Venusaur matched the opponent’s slow Trick Room core very well: sun enabled immediate Solar Beam pressure on Garganacl, Sleep Powder repeatedly denied Mimikyu and Slowking, and Kingambit cleanly exploited the Psychic/Ghost core once Trick Room was active. The opponent’s Wide Guard made spread Fire less reliable, but the team retained strong single-target answers in Solar Beam, Air Slash, Kowtow Cleave, and Iron Head. The between-game approach helped rather than backfired: bringing Charizard/Venusaur/Kingambit gave proactive anti-TR pressure and a favorable endgame, while Mega Evolving Charizard Y was correct for sun, Chlorophyll support, and Garganacl coverage. The main favorable swing was sleep disruption plus early Garganacl pressure; Stone Edge missing Charizard helped preserve the sun core, but the win was not solely dependent on it. Series prep was strong: the registered six contained the right anti-TR tools, especially Charizard Y, Venusaur, Kingambit, and Raichu. Dragonite, Altaria, Emolga, and Avalugg do not show a clearer matchup advantage over this revealed core; Avalugg especially risks passive play into special attackers and Trick Room, while the other omitted fliers overlap with Charizard’s role or face Mimikyu/Armarouge pressure.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series, retain the Charizard Y/Venusaur/Kingambit framework and strongly consider Raichu as the fourth to add Fake Out, Encore, Electroweb, and Lightning Rod utility against Trick Room attempts and special offense. Continue to Mega Evolve Charizard Y when Venusaur is brought unless preserving pre-Mega typing or speed has a specific tactical purpose. Lead with immediate anti-Trick Room pressure, but do not rely on repeated Sleep Powder misses or a Stone Edge miss: target Mimikyu decisively while respecting Mental Herb and Taunt, and keep Kingambit healthy enough to punish Slowking and Armarouge under Trick Room. Against Garganacl, favor Solar Beam, Energy Ball, Kowtow Cleave, and Iron Head over Heat Wave because Wide Guard is confirmed; account for Recover before assuming it is in finishing range.
reflections.notebook: Opponent favors a slow Trick Room structure: Mental Herb Mimikyu is a primary setter and carries Taunt, while Galarian Slowking is a secondary setter with Regenerator, Sitrus Berry, and Chilly Reception. Mimikyu’s Mental Herb does not prevent sleep; both Mimikyu and Slowking can be disrupted by Sleep Powder, though sleep is probabilistic and should not be the only TR answer. Armarouge is Quiet Life Orb Flash Fire with Armor Cannon, Expanding Force, Wide Guard, and Protect; avoid leaning on Fire damage into it and respect Wide Guard against spread attacks. Garganacl is Brave Leftovers Purifying Salt with Stone Edge, Salt Cure, Wide Guard, and Recover; pressure it with single-target Grass and Steel attacks, and plan for recovery. Tsareena is confirmed Choice Scarf with Queenly Majesty, so it can block priority; Scrafty is Brave Lum Berry Intimidate with Fake Out, Knock Off, Close Combat, and Ice Punch. Charizard Y/Venusaur/Kingambit is a proven favorable core into this composition: sun grants immediate Grass pressure and Chlorophyll tempo, while Kingambit punishes the opponent’s Psychic/Ghost pieces and remains useful when Trick Room goes up. Raichu is valuable support for a future rematch, particularly Fake Out/Encore speed control, but Queenly Majesty must be considered if Tsareena is present.
